basis: Partner sets are printed data, versioned with this file — not code comments. A partner country is 'exposed' for (reporter, chokepoint) when its primary container route to the reporter transits the chokepoint, expressed as region pairs seeded from the replay datasets' route structure (Red Sea 2024: Asia–Europe corridor via Bab el-Mandeb + Suez; Panama 2023-24: Asia ↔ US East/Gulf and Pacific Latin America routings) and canonical liner geography. Bilateral Comtrade data contains no routing; every Tier-2 figure derived from this file carries the MODELLED routing chip. Region membership below is UN M49 country codes for the principal trading partners; partners outside every region are never counted as exposed.

not_seeded.reason: Gibraltar transit applies to Mediterranean-facing European trade, but Comtrade reporters are whole countries (Spain, France, Italy report Atlantic + Mediterranean ports together); a country-level set would misattribute Atlantic-facing flows. Not seeded rather than misprinted.
Turkish Straits transit is dominated by Black Sea bulk (grain/energy) routings whose partner structure is bilateral and seasonal; no defensible standing partner set. Not seeded.
Danish Straits / Øresund transit is Baltic regional trade between neighbouring reporters; the exposure is already visible in Tier-1 port shares for Baltic ports. No separate routing set seeded.
Dover Strait traffic is intra-European short-sea and cross-Channel flow between adjacent reporters; a transit set would label nearly all intra-Europe trade as exposed, which says nothing. Not seeded.
Mozambique Channel routings are an alternative (Cape-route) corridor rather than a primary route for a definable partner set. Not seeded.
The Cape is the diversion route, not a primary route: partner flows are counted as exposed to the Cape only in a what-if, never as standing structure. Not seeded.

central_asia.label: Central Asia (landlocked reporters: no sea-route exposure set claims them; listed so reporter coverage is complete and their Tier-2 rows are empty by construction, not by omission)

latin_america.label: Latin America (incl. Pacific coast: Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia)

sets.basis: Asia–Europe container corridor: services between East/South/Southeast Asia and Oceania and North Europe transit Suez as the primary route (Red Sea replay structure). Gulf (Middle East) origins to Europe also route via Suez after Bab el-Mandeb.

Bab el-Mandeb is the Red Sea gate on the same Asia–Europe corridor as Suez (the Red Sea replay dataset treats the two as one corridor); every Suez Asia–Europe routing also transits Bab el-Mandeb, and Gulf–Europe routings join it after Hormuz.

Asia → US East/Gulf container services route via Panama as a primary routing; Pacific-coast Latin America (Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia) trades with North America and Europe via Panama. KNOWN LIMIT, printed with every Panama row: Comtrade reporters are whole countries — US imports from Asia include West Coast arrivals that do NOT transit Panama, so US-reporter Panama exposure is an upper bound, not a split.

Malacca is the primary strait between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea: East Asia's trade with Europe, South Asia, the Middle East and Africa transits it, as does Southeast Asia's trade with those regions.
All seaborne trade originating in Gulf states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait, Iraq, Iran) exits via Hormuz; every destination region is exposed for those origins.
Northeast Asia's trade with Southeast and South Asia routes through the Taiwan Strait / South China Sea corridor as the primary path; Oceania–East Asia services also pass it.

us_partner_codes_note: Partner records name the United States as 840 or 842 depending on the reporter's own convention; both codes are the United States for exposure matching.
